root_cause: Thyroid storm from untreated Graves' disease, triggered by stopping meds plus pseudoephedrine

patient.name: Maya Okafor
patient.background: Biology student, Graves' disease diagnosed last year, stopped methimazole months ago.

findings.result: Enlarged, hyperactive gland; very high free T4
Atrial fibrillation at 160 bpm, heart straining
Hot, soaking wet skin; shin swelling (pretibial myxedema)
Hyperactive bowel, no pathogens on stool culture
CT normal; no bleed or meningitis signs
High glucose, high white cells (leukocytosis), no bacteremia

treatments.name: Propranolol, PTU, iodine, steroids
treatments.why: Beta-blockade slows the heart, PTU blocks hormone production and T4-to-T3 conversion, iodine (given after PTU) stops release, and steroids lower conversion further.
treatments.attending_line: Look at that, you treated the gland instead of the symptoms. Mark the calendar.

treatments.name: Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
treatments.why: Fever and high white cells look like sepsis, but there's no infection, so the hormone surge keeps going.
treatments.attending_line: Great, the bacteria she doesn't have are terrified. Her thyroid isn't.

treatments.name: Aspirin for fever
treatments.why: Aspirin pushes thyroid hormone off its binding proteins, so more free hormone reaches the tissues and the storm gets worse.
treatments.attending_line: You freed more hormone. Bold choice, aiming the fire hose at the fire.

treatments.name: Electrical cardioversion only
treatments.why: Shocking her back to a normal rhythm won't last while thyroid hormone keeps driving the heart, and new AF clots can break loose.
treatments.attending_line: You rebooted the heart. The virus is still in the thyroid.

post_mortem: Maya had stopped taking her Graves' medicine, and the pseudoephedrine in her cold pills, plus exam stress, tipped her into thyroid storm. Sweating in a cold room, her history, and the shin swelling all pointed to the thyroid, not to food poisoning or sepsis.
